findings.where: Header nav ("Destinations", "How we rank", the MantaHostels wordmark) and footer links ("Privacy", "Terms", "How we rank", "Report content"), at both widths
findings.fault: The links go nowhere. "Destinations" points to #destinations, but this page has no such section. "How we rank", "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content" all point back to this page. The wordmark is labelled "MantaHostels home" but also points back to this page. Every way off the page except the email link reloads the page or does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who wants to compare other Bali spots, check how hostels are ranked or read the privacy terms taps the link and stays where they are. The site looks broken, on a product whose pitch is trust.

findings.where: "Good for" section: all twelve tags (First-time surfers, Remote workers, Long stays … Sunsets)
findings.fault: The tags are static, but they look like filter chips: a pill shape, a fill, a heavy border, in a row of options. On a hostel-search brand, visitors will read them as filters they can tap to narrow hostels, and tapping does nothing. Each tag also gets a different fill and border colour (yellow, green, pink, teal, purple) that means nothing. Some fills are coral-pink, the colour kept for the one call to action. So one look stands for many meanings it doesn't have.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone taps "Solo travellers" or "Budget" expecting matching hostels and gets nothing. They then guess at what the colours mean (is pink nightlife-only? is yellow a warning?).

findings.where: "Coming soon" notice above the footer, at both widths
findings.fault: The notice says Manta has no listings yet, but it sits on a saturated red ground. That is the look of an error or danger alert. Red here borrows the danger signifier for something that is not a status fault. The rules file gives this block the ink night ground.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scrolling to the end sees a red alert box and thinks something failed, such as the page or a booking. They stop trusting the guide above it at the moment the page explains why there are no hostels.

findings.fault: The heading is static, but it is set in a link colour with an underline (and in italics), so it looks like a link. The next heading, "Surf", is plain ink, so the difference suggests "Vibe" goes somewhere.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who taps "Vibe" expecting more on Canggu's social scene gets nothing. The underline also weakens the cue that real links use on this page.

findings.where: Page title "Best Hostels in Canggu", and the end of the page after the coming-soon notice
findings.fault: The title promises a ranked list of hostels, but the page has none. A visitor only learns this from the notice at the very bottom, and that notice offers no next step: no way to be told when listings go live, and no link to a destination that has listings. The page ends in a dead end.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrived from search to pick a Canggu hostel reads the whole guide expecting the list, finds there isn't one and has nothing to do but leave. The founder loses the visitor.
